atAGlance: Chả giò is Vietnamese fried spring rolls, usually with crisp shell, pork or mixed filling, lettuce, herbs, and fish sauce.
whatItIs: Chả giò are southern Vietnamese fried spring rolls, usually pork or mixed filling in a crisp wrapper, served with lettuce, herbs, and fish-sauce dip.
howToEnjoy: Wrap a hot fried roll in lettuce or herbs, then dip in the fish-sauce dip. The greens cool the fried shell and keep each bite fresh.
howLocalsOrder: Order chả giò as a shared starter or alongside bún. Ask for no chili in the fish-sauce dip and use the lettuce and herbs instead of eating the rolls plain.
worthKnowing: In southern Vietnam, chả giò is the fried-roll word visitors need; in the north, you may see nem rán for a similar idea.
goodToKnow: If sweet-sour fish-sauce dip comes separately, start with a small dip; it can be salty, sweet, sour, and spicy at once.
